lead: Kansas City plumbing deals with cold winters, hard river water, old basements and clay soil. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Kansas City.
risk: frozen pipes, basement sewer backups and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, sewer backups and old pipes
why: Brookside, Waldo, Westport and the Northeast have many homes from the early 1900s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Clay soil moves with the seasons and cracks them.
Older parts of the city have combined sewers that can back up into basements in heavy rain. Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls.
water: KC Water treats Missouri River water. River water is hard, and the utility softens it during treatment, but scale still builds up over time.
tips: Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in the Crossroads, Westport, Brookside, Waldo, the Plaza, the Northland and every other Kansas City neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Kansas City City Planning and Development Department, which also licenses plumbers in the city. Missouri has no statewide plumber license.

faq.q: Who licenses plumbers in Kansas City, Missouri?
faq.a: Missouri has no statewide plumber license, so Kansas City licenses plumbers through its City Planning and Development Department. Ask for the city license number before work starts.
